Stable Isotopes and General Transport Theory

Scope, component inventory, and certificate map

This page synthesizes two cross-cutting RELIC packages (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 23, 25, and 26):

  1. Stable-isotope fractionation and ledger lifecycle (relic.scientific.isotopes): stateless exact-partition binary fractionation calculators ([I]), the fail-closed Level 0 runtime boundary IsotopeHeartbeatFunctor ([N]), and the retired legacy pool-tracker status ([X]).

  2. General continuum and discrete cochain transport (relic.scientific.transport): finite-volume upwind advection, Fickian diffusion (at both Level 3 open boundaries and its Level 4 closed 1D dissipative port-Hamiltonian runtime point), and operator-split advection-diffusion.

Across these two packages, four concrete scientific Functors carry five declarative IPHSEquivalenceCertificate files (four primary class certificates plus one secondary Level 4 constructor-conditioned certificate on FickianDiffusion):

Stable-isotope ratios, exact binary fractionation, and fail-closed ledger status

Ratio, fractional abundance, and delta notation

For a binary isotope pair with heavy amount \(M_h \ge 0\) and strictly positive light amount \(M_l > 0\) (for example \(^{13}\mathrm{C}/^{12}\mathrm{C}\), \(^{15}\mathrm{N}/^{14}\mathrm{N}\), or \(^{18}\mathrm{O}/^{16}\mathrm{O}\)), the isotope ratio \(R\), heavy and light fractional abundances \((x_h, x_l)\), and per-mil \(\delta\) value relative to international reference ratio \(R_{\mathrm{std}}\) (VPDB, AIR-\(\mathrm{N}_2\), or VSMOW; Fry, 2006; Sharp, 2017) satisfy

\[ R = \frac{M_h}{M_l}, \qquad x_h = \frac{M_h}{M_h + M_l} = \frac{R}{1 + R}, \qquad x_l = \frac{M_l}{M_h + M_l} = \frac{1}{1 + R}, \qquad \delta = \left(\frac{R}{R_{\mathrm{std}}} - 1\right)\times 1000\quad [\text{per mil}]. \]

Because \(\delta\) is a nonlinear ratio transform and lacks extensive additivity, mixing two reservoirs \(A\) and \(B\) conserves heavy and light masses separately (\(M_h = M_{h,A} + M_{h,B}\), \(M_l = M_{l,A} + M_{l,B}\)); a total-mass-weighted average of \(\delta\) is only a small-\(R\) approximation. Zero or negative light-isotope denominators raise a domain error without masking depletion behind arbitrary regularizers.

Stateless exact binary rational fractionation calculators ([I])

relic.scientific.isotopes.fractionation implements stateless calculation utilities (IsotopeFractionationCalculator, Carbon13FractionationCalculator, Nitrogen15FractionationCalculator, and Oxygen18FractionationCalculator, all [I]). Given product-to-substrate fractionation factor \(\alpha = R_p / R_s > 0\) (related to per-mil enrichment by \(\varepsilon = (\alpha - 1)\times 1000\) and kinetic isotope effect \(\mathrm{KIE} = k_l / k_h\)), a total elemental flux \(F\) leaving a donor pool of ratio \(R_s\) carries product ratio \(R_F = \alpha R_s\) and is partitioned via the exact binary rational formulas:

\[ F_h = F\,\frac{\alpha R_s}{1 + \alpha R_s}, \qquad F_l = F\,\frac{1}{1 + \alpha R_s}, \qquad F_h + F_l = F. \]

Unlike the trace-abundance linearization \(F_h \approx \alpha R_s F\), exact rational partitioning preserves total elemental mass \(F_h + F_l = F\) identically for all \(R_s \ge 0\) and \(\alpha > 0\). The calculators also provide closed-system Rayleigh substrate evolution \(R(f)/R_0 = f^{\alpha - 1}\) for remaining fraction \(f \in (0, 1]\), Farquhar et al. (1982) \(\mathrm{C_3}\) photosynthetic \(^{13}\mathrm{C}\) discrimination

\[ \Delta_{\mathrm{C_3}} = a + (b - a)\,\frac{c_i}{c_a}, \]

Mariotti et al. (1981) nitrogen kinetic fractionation relations, and Craig and Gordon (1965) evaporative \(^{18}\mathrm{O}\) vapor-ratio closures

\[ R_E = \frac{R_L / \alpha_{\mathrm{eq}}(T) - h\,R_A - \varepsilon_k R_L}{1 - h + \varepsilon_k}. \]

Fail-closed IsotopeHeartbeatFunctor ([N]) and retired MultiIsotopePoolTracker ([X])

Prognostic multi-pool isotope state coupling across arbitrary Functor graphs is intentionally fail-closed until full component UpdateItem bindings, parent process ownership, and checkpoint-replay contracts are wired:

  • relic.scientific.isotopes.functor.IsotopeHeartbeatFunctor (Level 0, [N]) and relic.scientific.isotopes.wire_isotope_tracker reject execution before any simulator or StateManager mutation with runtime_unbound.

  • The historical out-of-band MultiIsotopePoolTracker class has been deleted ([X]) because mutating private pool dictionaries outside StateManager violated single-writer provenance and conservation auditing.

General conservative transport Functors

All three Functors in relic.scientific.transport inherit TransportMechanismFunctor, assemble oriented face fluxes on finite-volume cochain complexes, emit integrated concentration increments via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True), and account explicitly for boundary fluxes and any configured non-negativity clipping residual \(R_{\mathrm{clip}}\) in the discrete volume ledger

\[ \sum_i V_i c_i^{n+1} - \sum_i V_i c_i^n = -\Delta t \sum_{f \in \partial\Omega} A_f q_f + \Delta t \sum_i V_i s_i + R_{\mathrm{clip}}. \]

Finite-volume upwind linear advection (LinearAdvection, Level 3)

relic.scientific.transport.advection.LinearAdvection (Level 3) discretizes \(\partial_t c + \nabla \cdot (\mathbf{v} c) = s\) with oriented upwind face fluxes (LeVeque, 2002):

\[\begin{split} \frac{\mathrm{d}c_i}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\frac{q_{i+1/2} - q_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x_i} + s_i, \qquad q_{i+1/2} = \begin{cases} v_{i+1/2}\,c_i, & v_{i+1/2} \ge 0,\\ v_{i+1/2}\,c_{i+1}, & v_{i+1/2} < 0, \end{cases} \end{split}\]

enforcing the ParameterManager-governed advective Courant limit \(\mathrm{CFL} = \max_i (\lvert v_i \rvert \Delta t / \Delta x_i) \le \mathrm{CFL}_{\max}\) and distinguishing periodic, closed no-flux wall, Dirichlet, Neumann, and open inflow/outflow boundary contracts.

Fickian diffusion: Level-3 general operator and Level-4 dissipative port-Hamiltonian point

  1. General multi-dimensional open/bounded mode (FickianDiffusion, Level 3): relic.scientific.transport.diffusion.FickianDiffusion discretizes \(\partial_t c = \nabla \cdot (\mathbf{K}\nabla c) + s\) in cochain form \(\dot{\mathbf{c}}_h = -D_h \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{diff},h} + G_h \mathbf{u}_h\) with harmonic face diffusivity \(\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{diff},h} = -\star_K d_h \mathbf{c}_h\) (\(\star_K = \star_K^{\mathsf{T}} \succeq 0\)) and explicit diffusion stability audit \(\mu = K \Delta t / \Delta x^2 \le \mu_{\max}\) across 1D, 2D, and 3D supports (Crank, 1975).

  2. Closed 1D source-free dissipative port-Hamiltonian runtime point (Level 4): Under the secondary constructor-conditioned certificate constructor_selection = {strict_runtime_point: True, spatial_dims: 1} (FickianDiffusion strict runtime point, Level 4), FickianDiffusion restricts execution to a closed (periodic or zero-flux wall) 1D uniform grid of spacing \(\Delta x\) with zero boundary ports (\(G_h = 0\)) and fail-closed rejection of any nonzero source_term. Binding the quadratic \(L^2\) storage functional and autograd effort covector

    \[H_h(\mathbf{c}_h) = \frac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{c}_h^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{c}_h, \qquad \mathbf{e}_H = \frac{\partial H_h}{\partial \mathbf{c}_h} = \mathbf{c}_h,\]

    the production finite-volume diffusion drift coincides identically with the canonical dissipative port-Hamiltonian structure (\(J_h = 0\)):

    \[\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{c}_h}{\mathrm{d}t} = (J_h - R_h)\,\mathbf{e}_H = -R_h\,\mathbf{c}_h, \qquad R_h = \frac{1}{\Delta x^2}\,d_h^{\mathsf{T}}\operatorname{diag}(K_f)\,d_h = R_h^{\mathsf{T}} \succeq 0,\]

    satisfying monotone storage dissipation

    \[\frac{\mathrm{d}H_h}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\mathbf{e}_H^{\mathsf{T}} R_h\,\mathbf{e}_H = -\sum_f K_f\left(\frac{\Delta_f c_h}{\Delta x}\right)^2 \le 0\]

    and exact discrete mass conservation \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}} R_h \mathbf{c}_h = 0\). On every emitted step in this configuration, forward() executes relic.computation.operators.iphs.IPHSStructureSpec.validate at required_level = 4 and records the live audit on last_strict_iphs_audit (van der Schaft and Jeltsema, 2014). Because no thermodynamic entropy functional \(S_h\) or reversible-irreversible GENERIC cross-degeneracy is claimed for isothermal tracer diffusion, the certificate terminates at Level 4 (with Level 5 reserved for GENERIC entropy-coupled formulations).

Combined advection-diffusion and operator-splitting accuracy (AdvectionDiffusion, Level 3)

relic.scientific.transport.advection_diffusion.AdvectionDiffusion (Level 3) combines advective and diffusive cochain sub-flows (\(\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{v}c - \mathbf{K}\nabla c\), cell Peclet diagnostic \(\mathrm{Pe} = \lvert \mathbf{v} \rvert \Delta x / K\)) via configurable sequential ("sequential" Lie-Trotter, \(\Phi_D^{\Delta t}\circ \Phi_A^{\Delta t}\)) or symmetric ("symmetric" Strang, \(\Phi_D^{\Delta t/2}\circ \Phi_A^{\Delta t}\circ \Phi_D^{\Delta t/2}\)) operator splitting (Hundsdorfer and Verwer, 2003):

  • Symmetric Strang composition eliminates the leading first-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff commutator \([A, D]\Delta t^2 / 2\), achieving \(O(\Delta t^2)\) splitting commutator error when paired with second-order sub-flow integrators such as "implicit_midpoint".

  • Under the default first-order explicit "euler" sub-integrators, local sub-step truncation error is \(O(\Delta t^2)\) per step, so the composite AdvectionDiffusion trajectory remains globally first-order \(O(\Delta t)\) even when "symmetric" splitting is selected.

When transporting stable isotopes across spatial grids, callers transport the conserved heavy and light concentrations \((c_h, c_l)\) and reconstruct \(\delta\) diagnostically after transport, avoiding direct advection or diffusion of non-conservative \(\delta\) values.

  • Bird, R. B., Stewart, W. E., and Lightfoot, E. N. (2007). Transport Phenomena (2nd ed.). Wiley.

  • Craig, H. and Gordon, L. I. (1965). Deuterium and oxygen-18 variations in the ocean and the marine atmosphere. In Stable Isotopes in Oceanographic Studies and Paleotemperatures, CNR Laboratorio di Geologia Nucleare, Pisa, 9-130.

  • Crank, J. (1975). The Mathematics of Diffusion (2nd ed.). Oxford University Press.

  • Farquhar, G. D., O’Leary, M. H., and Berry, J. A. (1982). On the relationship between carbon isotope discrimination and the intercellular carbon dioxide concentration in leaves. Australian Journal of Plant Physiology, 9, 121-137.

  • Fry, B. (2006). Stable Isotope Ecology. Springer.

  • Hundsdorfer, W. and Verwer, J. G. (2003). Numerical Solution of Time-Dependent Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations. Springer.

  • LeVeque, R. J. (2002). Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems. Cambridge University Press.

  • Mariotti, A. et al. (1981). Experimental determination of nitrogen kinetic isotope fractionation: some principles; illustration for the denitrification and nitrification processes. Plant and Soil, 62, 413-430.

  • Sharp, Z. (2017). Principles of Stable Isotope Geochemistry (2nd ed.). Prentice Hall / Open Educational Edition.
